INTERNAL REVENUE SERVICE — INDEPENDENT OFFICE OF APPEALS
Appeals Case Memorandum (Summary)

Taxpayers: Michael A. Okafor and Diane R. Okafor
Tax Year: 2022
Appeals Officer: T. Nakamura
Conference Date: February 11, 2025
Protest Filed: November 20, 2024

Issues Considered

1. Unreported income — bank deposits method ($47,600 as determined in RAR)
2. Disallowed vehicle expense ($9,800)
3. Disallowed home office expense ($4,200)
4. Disallowed contract labor expense ($4,400)
5. Accuracy-related penalty under IRC Section 6662(a)

Determination

1. Unreported income: Taxpayers submitted a CPA-prepared reconciliation (dated May 19, 2025 —
   received informally prior to formal issuance but discussed at conference) identifying $23,200
   as a transfer between the taxpayers' own accounts and $14,000 as repayment of a personal loan.
   Supporting bank statements for the savings transfer were provided and appear to corroborate the
   $23,200 item. Documentation for the $14,000 loan repayment (promissory note, cancelled checks)
   was incomplete at the time of this conference — taxpayers produced an unsigned draft of a
   promissory note but no contemporaneous evidence the funds were actually advanced in 2021.
   Appeals is not sustaining the $23,200 adjustment based on the savings-account documentation, but
   is sustaining the remaining $24,400 ($14,000 loan item plus $6,200 duplicate-deposit item plus
   $4,200 unreconciled item) pending further documentation, which may still be submitted to Tax
   Court counsel.

2. Vehicle expense: Partial contemporaneous log for July–December 2022 was provided. Appeals will
   allow a corrected deduction of $152 for the documented period; the undocumented January–June
   portion remains disallowed for lack of contemporaneous records under IRC Section 274(d).

3. Home office expense: Appeals accepts the corrected calculation of $917 (10 months at 10.5% of
   home square footage, simplified method) in place of the original $4,200 claim.

4. Contract labor: No additional documentation was provided. This $4,400 adjustment is sustained
   in full.

5. Accuracy-related penalty: Given the taxpayers' engagement of a CPA, partial cooperation during
   the exam, and partial substantiation obtained on review, Appeals will recommend the penalty be
   asserted only against the portion of the deficiency that is ultimately sustained, rather than
   the full amount originally proposed, consistent with a reasonable-cause and reliance-on-
   preparer argument under IRC Section 6664(c). Full resolution of the penalty is deferred pending
   the Tax Court's determination on the underlying deficiency, as the case has already been
   petitioned.

Note: This is a summary Appeals memorandum, not a closing agreement. The matter remains pending
before the United States Tax Court under the petition filed June 30, 2025.
